extracted.intended_audience: researchers/educated public interested in child language development (linguists, psychologists, child observers)
extracted.subtask_description: Longitudinal, observational notes on a single infant's language acquisition, with recommendations and exemplars for transcription, interpretation, and selection of observations. Emphasises order of acquisition, consistent phonetic notation, and preserving contemporaneous records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record only directly observed facts
rubrics_metrics.description: “I think I have set down nothing as fact which has not been actually and distinctly observed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report only items that were actually and distinctly observed at the time; avoid asserting conjectures as facts. If interpretation is offered, distinguish it from the raw observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize order of acquisition over precise ages
rubrics_metrics.description: “Exact dates I have not attempted to give, conceiving that they would be of no use unless for the comparison of a very large number of observations. Children differ so much in forwardness that the time of particular acquisitions seems of little importance as compared with their order.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting developmental milestones, emphasize the sequence in which items are acquired rather than absolute calendar ages, unless you have a large comparative sample where timing is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent phonetic transcription and explain conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: “Though I have no pretensions to skill in phonetics, I thought it at least desirable to use some consistent notation for the sounds actually produced. For this purpose I have taken the Indian Government system, with a few additional signs which will speak for themselves. Words in italics are in the Indian Government spelling. Words between inverted commas are in ordinary English spelling.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a single, explicit transcription system for the sounds produced; document any deviations or additional signs and state typographic conventions (italics, quotation marks) so readers can interpret examples reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve contemporaneous records; minimise retouching
rubrics_metrics.description: “I have retouched and rearranged them as little as possible, preferring the certainty of leaving them in an inartificial state to the risk of spoiling by manipulation whatever value they may possess as records made at the time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep field notes and examples as close to their original form as possible; avoid editing or rephrasing that could alter the meaning or contextual cues of the original observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate intentional use from mere vocal exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation example: bd bd was sometimes ‘a sort of general demonstrative’ or an interjection, but 'both sounds, however, seemed often to be made without distinct intention, as mere exercise of the vocal organs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding or interpreting infant utterances, note whether a sound appears used with communicative intent (consistent referential use) or appears as non-intentional vocal play; annotate ambiguous cases rather than forcing an interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include prosody, tone, and gestures in interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The child 'fills up the meaning of her syllables with a great variety of tone, and also with inarticulate interjections. Impatience, satisfaction, disappointment, amusement, are all very well marked.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record not only segmental phonetic forms but also intonation, prosodic patterns, and accompanying gestures or facial expressions, since these convey communicative meaning especially in early stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for individual variability; avoid overgeneralization from a single case
rubrics_metrics.description: “Children differ so much in forwardness that the time of particular acquisitions seems of little importance…” and the author repeatedly notes that some features may be idiosyncratic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat findings from a single child as exemplars rather than universal norms; explicitly flag which observations may be individual-specific and avoid broad generalizations without corroborating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document semantic extension and usage (how words are generalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: the child uses 'bd bd' as demonstrative and interjection; 'Bessie' is used generically for multiple dolls; 'bacon' initially generalised to breakfast dishes then partitioned into egg, bacon, fish, beef.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record not just form but the meanings assigned by the child and any extensions/generalizations (e.g., generic uses, overextensions, semantic narrowing), with concrete examples showing contexts of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track phonetic/phonological development and substitution patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: The notes catalogue which vowels and consonants are 'under command' (e.g., a, i), which consonants are not yet formed (g, l, r, sibilants, aspirates, palatals), common substitutions (r→l, th→s or z), and emergence of final consonants and dissyllables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically record presence/absence of phonemes, typical substitution errors, emergence of final consonants and multisyllabic forms; present chronological snapshots to show progression of articulatory competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record dialogic turns and emergent conversational competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Author notes first sustained conversation and repartee (e.g., 'Dirty!' — 'Clean!'), appearance of questions ('Where's pussy?'), and ability to answer direct questions with intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples of multi-turn exchanges, question forms, replies, and pretend dialogue with dolls to document onset of conversational and pragmatic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use selective sampling when continuous recording is impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: “After this time the child's progress became much more rapid, and it would not have been possible to take down all her new words without giving much more and more continuous attention than I had at my disposal... The subsequent notes must be taken as being rather selections than a full record.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When continuous exhaustive transcription is infeasible, use clearly-labelled selective sampling (noting selection criteria) and acknowledge gaps; focus on representative examples across domains (phonology, lexicon, syntax, pragmatics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate inferred meanings and explain interpretive uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the notes the author often adds queries or qualifications (e.g., 'I noted, however, with a query, man as a second and specialized meaning'), and points out where an utterance 'seemed' to mean something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inferring meanings or functions for child utterances, explicitly mark uncertainties and the basis for inference (context, repetition, adult modelling), so readers can assess the strength of interpretive claims.
